title: Surrey man dies in police custody
article: A 22-year-old Surrey man died in police custody Thursday night following a drug bust in Whalley.
RCMP have identified Brandon Whitelaw as the deceased, a man they say was known to police.
At around 4:30 p.m., RCMP were investigating suspected drug trafficking at a residence in the Ravine Road area they identified as a notorious crack house.
A vehicle that left the scene was followed by police and subsequently stopped near 106 Avenue and 132 Street for minor "driving infractions."
An investigation ensued, during which RCMP say they observed "evidence of narcotics" in the vehicle.
The vehicle's two occupants were asked to step out of the car and were arrested for drugs. (The other man, the driver, was later released with no charges.)
Shortly after being handcuffed, Whitelaw went into what police are calling "medical distress," suffering from an apparent airway obstruction.
The officers began emergency treatment at the scene, and were ultimately relieved by fire department crews and paramedics.
Ambulance attendants recovered an intact plastic bag from Whitelaw's airway, which police later found contained 11 rocks of crack cocaine.
Whitelaw was transported to Surrey Memorial Hospital where he died a short time later.
The Integrated Homicide Investigation Team has taken over the investigation.
There will also be separate investigations by the Commission of Public Complaints Against the RCMP as well as an independent officer review of the incident.
Whitelaw is the third man to die in Surrey RCMP custody in the past six weeks.
On July 1, Ryan Wagemans, 24, of Langley died in hospital after he was involved in a scuffle with security on a Coast Mountain bus and was subsequently restrained by RCMP officers.
June 19, David Stitt, 46, died in hospital after an altercation with police at a residence on Crescent Road.
